Oshodi. 6pm. The bus stop is full. The conductor is shouting. But the door is jammed.

That's most coaches and course creators running ads right now. The ads bring people to the bus stop. The leaks stop them getting in.

Swipe to find the leak jamming your door. Then comment your number, 1 to 5, and I'll reply with the first fix.

#onlinecoach #coursecreator #coachingbusiness #salesfunnel #lagoslogic
alts: Slide 1 of 10. For coaches and course creators running ads Your ads are not the problem. Your danfo door is jammed. Illustration: a yellow Lagos danfo bus with its door taped shut, a conductor shouting and a crowd waiting at the bus stop.

Slide 2 of 10. Picture this Oshodi. 6pm. Everybody wants to go home. So what does the conductor do? The conductor is shouting "Oshodi! Oshodi!" The bus stop is full. People are ready. But the door is jammed.
Slide 3 of 10. That's what raising your ad budget is. He shouts louder. Paying more money to shout at people who still can't get in. More budget. More clicks. Same empty cohort.

Slide 4 of 10. Before you buy more fuel Ad money is fuel. Fuel is expensive. Swipe. Count your leaks. Every funnel is a danfo. Before you spend one more naira on ads, check the 5 places your passengers fall off.

Slide 5 of 10. The conductor shouts "Enter! Enter!" but never says where the bus is going. Your ad says "Transform your life in 90 days." Nobody can tell if this bus is for them. Shout the destination: who it is for, what they get.
Slide 6 of 10. The bus looks like one chance. No face. No student results. Just "life changing" and a countdown timer. Nobody enters a bus they don't trust. Show proof before you ask for money.

Slide 7 of 10. The door is jammed. "DM for details." A 12 question form. A payment link that fails on phones. They wanted to enter. You made it hard. Every extra step = one passenger walking to the next bus.

Slide 8 of 10. The passenger said "Wait, make I buy gala." The bus zoomed off. "Let me check my account." "I'll join the next cohort." Then you never messaged again. "I'll get back to you" is not a no.

Slide 9 of 10. The driver doesn't know which route pays. You ran five ads. You can't say which one brought your students. So you keep paying for the empty route. Ask every buyer: where did you hear about us?

text:
Most coaches and course creators think their ads are the problem.

Usually the ads are working. People arrive. Then they hit one of five leaks: the message, trust, friction, follow up or measurement.

I explained it with the most Lagos thing I know: a danfo with a jammed door.

Which leak costs your business the most?

Buyers have a name for your sales page: word salad.

“Can anyone look at this sales page and tell me ONE thing you'll actually learn?!” That's a real buyer on Reddit, talking about a coach's program.

The fix: one concrete promise per section. A number, a timeline, a real example.

Paste your headline below and I'll tell you if it's word salad.

Slide 2 of 8. What they say Quote from Reddit user, r/LifeCoachSnark: Here's the sales page for [a coach's] new ROI program….can anyone look at this sales page and tell me ONE thing you'll actually learn?!
Slide 3 of 8. And Quote from Reddit user, r/LifeCoachSnark: Is the sales page word salad or actually listing tangible results?
Slide 4 of 8. What they want “Tell me ONE thing I'll actually learn.” Not transformation. Not “unlock your potential”. One concrete thing.

Slide 5 of 8. Example Word salad vs a real promise Word salad: “Unlock your full potential and step into your next level with our transformational program.” Real promise: “In 4 weeks you'll write and send your first 3 sales emails, with my feedback on each.”

Slide 6 of 8. The word salad test Check every section Could a stranger say what they'll get after reading it? Is there a number: weeks, lessons, a price? Is there proof: a real student, a screenshot, a sample? Would you say this sentence out loud to a friend?
Slide 7 of 8. The rule One concrete promise per section. Specific sounds honest. Vague sounds like a scam.
